What this board is, and what it is not

PROVISIONAL. These are M-C candidates tested by the corrected incumbent against a declared opponent panel. No rating is published and no strength claim is made.

  • 410 candidates over 6560 qualified native matches. The cards carry 7600 team records of those matches, because 1040 of them are the OTHER side of games a contender played from an opponent seat — recovered from retained receipts, not replayed. One match is still one match.
  • Player champions-incumbent-open-sheet-v1, information mode open-sheet, lineage 7428a95979e1. This incumbent sees open sheets: it is not playing under tournament information limits.
  • Opponents are a declared panel of 4 teams, selected before any candidate existed. Two are fixed references in every generation and two rotate (one revalidated historical archetype, one of the ladder's own survivors), so 109 distinct opponents have been faced across 82 committed generation(s). Only the reference record is comparable across generations: a 10–0 against one rotating pair is not better than 8–2 against another.
  • No ratings. Ratings stay off because this evidence does not support one: the opposition is a small, adaptively reused TRAINING panel, so a number here would read as a strength claim the games cannot carry. The games themselves are policy-qualified; it is the comparison that is narrow. A blank rating is a decision, not a gap in the data.
  • An M-B result cannot become a current M-C standing. The M-B board remains available and is not republished here. Open the Regulation M-B board — it is a different regulation and a different player, kept as history.
